Let the world know of 1971 genocide
2023-10-01T00:00:00+06:00 | Staff Correspondent
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/let-the-world-know-1971-genocide-3431486

It is important to effectively communicate the severity of the genocide carried out by the Pakistani occupation army on Bangalees during the 1971 Liberation War to the global community, said national and international researchers at an event yesterday.

While participating in an international seminar on genocide, they said  excluding genocide from the narrative would render it impossible to fully comprehend the sacrifices made by the nation's freedom-loving people during the nine-month struggle for independence.

"The 1971: Genocide-Torture Archive and Museum" organised the international seminar titled "Remembering genocide and Liberation War 1971: in the quest of diversity".

Speaking at the event, State Minister for Cultural Affairs KM Khalid said the Pakistani forces perpetrated one of the worst genocides in 1971. He expressed disappointment that some individuals continue to dispute the number of martyrs, highlighting the unique responsibility of researchers in addressing this issue.

"If the Liberation War or genocide issue  is limited within the country's borders, then the vastness of the war will be narrowed," he said.

Prof Sajal Nag from Assam University in India delivered the keynote paper during the inaugural session.

The event also featured addresses from Prof Muntassir Mamoon, the chairman of The 1971: Genocide-Torture Archive and Museum trustee board, as well as its trustee Chowdhury Shahid Kader and other participants.

At the opening session, filmmaker Kawsar Chowdhury and Calcutta University researcher Punam Mukharjee handed over rare collections of videos and photos of the Liberation War to the museum authority.

The museum's website was also launched during the event.
